reproduce.version_requirement: Reported PowerToys baseline and the affected WeChat version
prerequisites: Use only the minimal Ctrl/Alt exchange; record the exact WeChat version.
Use non-sensitive text and keep WeChat Alt+C enabled for the baseline.
reproduce.expected_result: No unintended window action occurs, and the evidence identifies whether the copy-to-close hypothesis explains each reported sequence.
steps: Double-click text and drag a selection separately; record copy, close and minimize behavior.
Compare with Keyboard Manager disabled and with only WeChat Alt+C disabled, one change at a time.
Maintainer traces distinguish physical keys, foreign injected keys and Keyboard Manager own injected marker; compare against a plain text application.

known_information: The reports describe WeChat minimizing or closing during drag/double-click when Ctrl and Alt are exchanged.

A commenter reports that WeChat-generated Ctrl+C becomes Alt+C and disabling WeChat Alt+C prevents closing, but did not observe the original copy behavior.

inferences: Remapping another application injected shortcut may explain the close action, but no trace establishes that as the complete original cause.

plan: Reproduce double-click and drag separately with one minimal Ctrl/Alt exchange and record the WeChat version.
Capture maintainer-side virtual-key/flags/extra-info ordering for physical and application-generated events without recording text.

proposed_fixes.title: Bound WeChat synthetic-shortcut interaction
proposed_fixes.root_cause: WeChat may synthesize a copy shortcut that Ctrl/Alt exchange turns into its close shortcut; event provenance and the original drag/minimize behavior remain unconfirmed.
verification: The original mouse sequence does not unexpectedly close/minimize WeChat while intended Ctrl/Alt remapping still works.
Copy behavior, unrelated applications and deliberate remapped injected input remain compatible.
